name: The Firm Knapsack Problem
description:
Problem L — The Firm Knapsack Problem
Contest: 2020-2021 Russia Team Open, High School Programming Contest (VKOSHP 20)

You are given a competitive programming problem requiring efficient evaluation under strict time and memory constraints.
The problem requires computing the optimal result using DSU on Tree and Small to Large Merging over the given input data.

Determine the optimal answer for each test case or query as specified below.
input_specification:
The first line contains an integer $T$ ($1 \le T \le 10^4$), representing the number of test cases (or $N$ for single-test problems).
The first line of each test case contains integers $N$ ($1 \le N \le 2 \times 10^5$) and additional parameters.
The second line contains $N$ space-separated integers $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_N$ ($1 \le a_i \le 10^9$).
output_specification:
For each test case, output the calculated answer on a single line.
If multiple valid solutions exist, output any of them. If the result can be large, compute it modulo $10^9 + 7$ (or $998244353$).
subsubtopic: 86. DSU on Tree and Small to Large Merging
approach_summary: Apply DSU on Tree and Small to Large Merging to maintain optimal invariant under contest constraints.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: gym_102893_L — The Firm Knapsack Problem [86. DSU on Tree and Small to Large Merging]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Connectivity is an equivalence relation. By organizing connected components into trees and merging smaller trees into larger ones (`union-by-rank/size`) combined with path compression, find and union operations run in near-constant inverse Ackermann time $O(\alpha(N))$.
